subject: Mean density for samples  pooled over 4 line transect surveys

messages.author: bca7a8f9317fbadd
messages.subject: Mean density for samples  pooled over 4 line transect surveys
parts:
Hi Listers
(Please reply directly to my email: jsin...@utas.edu.au)

My research project (Honours) consisted of comparing monitoring techniques (walked line transects, scat counts & spotlight strip transect surveys) for three macropod species on Maria Island National Park, Tasmania that have all been introduced and are annually culled. Cull estimates are currently derived from spotlight survey counts (not standardised) so that having a repeatable sampling technique for density estimates is vitally important.

I am having difficulty determining the mean density for Tasmanian pademelon (Thylogale billardierii) pooled over four line transect surveys undertaken a month apart. Sample sizes for individual sightings were small so I have manually pooled the data (total n = 60) and analysed through the DISTANCE program using Conventional Distance Sampling Analysis (self-taught!).

The default model was a half-normal key function with two cosine adjustments as the series expansion. The data was subsequently truncated at 80 m to improve the shoulder and reduce the peak at close distances with the following results:

Global density estimate

Effort : 21043.00
# samples : 16
Width : 80.00000
# observations: 59

Model 2
Half-normal key, k(y) = Exp(-y**2/(2*A(1)**2))
Cosine adjustments of order(s) : 2

Point Standard Percent Coef. 95% Percent
Parameter Estimate Error of Variation Confidence Interval
--------- ----------- ----------- -------------- ----------------------
D 0.71910 0.57635 80.15 0.16069 3.2181
N 1213.0 972.20 80.15 271.00 5429.0
--------- ----------- ----------- -------------- ----------------------

Detection probability
Estimate %CV df 95% Confidence Interval
------------------------------------------------------
Half-normal/Cosine
m 2.0000
LnL -212.82
AIC 429.65
AICc 429.86
BIC 433.80
Chi-p 0.45038
f(0) 0.51295E-01 8.34 57.00 0.43415E-01 0.60606E-01
p 0.24369 8.34 57.00 0.20625 0.28792
ESW 19.495 8.34 57.00 16.500 23.034

The question is how do I calculate the mean density estimate for Tasmanian pademelons from the count (N = 1213) of pooled data??

Regards
Janeane Ingram
Please reply directly to my email: jsin...@utas.edu.au
